successors.name: Jin dynasty (Jurchen Jin)
successors.text: eastern and northern Manchuria outside the Liao's land: the Jurchen country of Heilongjiang and Jilin

ledger.x: 1104: 'The Wanyan clan enters Goryeo territory in pursuit of enemy tribes, defeats Im Gan, and takes Chongju castle' (Timeline page); the Jurchen page: 'In 1104, the Wanyan Jurchens reached Chongju'.

December 1107: 'A Goryeo invasion led by Yun Kwan enters Jurchen territory and builds the Nine Fortresses in the area' (Timeline page); 'In December 1107, Yun Kwan and O Yonch'on set out with 170,000 soldiers' (Jurchen page).

1108: 'Goryeo returns the Nine Fortresses region to the Wanyan clan, possibly in exchange for Poju (Uiju), and Yun Kwan is removed from office' (Timeline page); the goryeo dossier records the matching loss.
1108: the Goryeo-Jurchen fighting ends with the return of the Nine Fortresses (the goryeo dossier runs the war to 1109 on its infobox).
November 1114: the Jurchens take Ningjiangzhou and win at Chuhedian.
January 1115: the Jin is proclaimed; the war with the Liao passes to the great-jin dossier.

wars.name: Jurchen-Goryeo war
wars.outcome: 1104: the Wanyan clan took Chongju and beat Im Gan; December 1107: Yun Kwan's 170,000 men built the Nine Fortresses; 1108: Goryeo returned the Nine Fortresses region to the Wanyan clan.

wars.name: Jurchen revolt against the Liao
wars.outcome: September 1114 Aguda rallied 2,500 men at Liushui and rebelled; November 1114 he took Ningjiangzhou and beat 7,000 Liao at Chuhedian; January 1115 he proclaimed the Jin.

certainty.note: Forest and river-valley tribal land; no page opened gives a boundary or an area.
